title: Nicewell Food Scale, 22lb Digital Kitchen Scale Weight Grams and oz for Cooking Baking, 1g/0.1oz Precise Graduation, Stainless Steel and Tempered Glass (Ash Silver)
description:
About this item
PRECISE WEIGHT： The digital food scale built-in four high-precision load sensors, quickly and accurately response 1g or 0.1oz increments when adding ingredients, its measuring range: 0.1oz to 22 lbs and 3g to 10kg(Min. weigh at 0.1oz or 3g)
MULTIFUNCTION LARGE SCALE：9"x6.3" platform and Large lcd display for easy readout in g, kg, lb: oz, fl.oz and ml. This digital weight scale is for better cooking, baking, tracking intake, weight loss and postage
PRACTICAL DESIGN： The food scale is designed with tempered glass for strong bearing, sleek stainless steel top surface for anti-fingerprint and easy clean, with a attached hook for convenient storage. REMINDING: there is a blue color protective film on the top to prevent from scratches, just tear off before use.
EASY TARE / ZERO OUT： Convenient tare button for tare calculation allows you to subtract the weight of plate or container, making it easy to achieve accurate readouts of ingredients
GREAT SUPPORT：2 AAA batteries included. We are always stand behind our kitchen scales, please feel free to reach to us if you have any issues

reviews_1s:
LOVED this scale until I realized how inaccurate it is. I have been using a food scale to track macros and aid in weight loss. I have successfully lost 80lbs with another 100 to go. I decided to “upgrade” and treat myself to a new scale, and purchased this one at the very end of January. Suddenly, my weight loss stalled and I couldn’t figure out why. I track and log EVERYTHING. Suddenly during March and April hadn’t lost anything. This morning I weighed out a portion of Cheerios, and I noticed that 30g seemed to be a whole lot more than I was used to seeing in the bowl. I pulled out my old scale, and the same portion came out to be 80g. I tested both scales with a variety of things, and found that this scale was doubling or even tripling the weights of everything. This explains why I have been maintaining, and not losing weight. 2 months of progress has been lost, and I was feeling very discouraged about it thinking that I hit a never ending plateau and even lowering my calories with no success. Thankful to have figured out the problem before I fully gave up. I’ll stick to my $10 scale as it seems to be more accurate.This scale is highly inaccurate. I weighed a can of soup with a net weight of 18.8 oz, so it should weigh more than that. One scale weighed it at 21.5 ounces, understandable since the soup is in a heavy can. This nicewell scale weighed the contents and can at only 12.8 ounces, off by almost half! I weighed several other items with known weights with the same inaccuracy. In all cases, I tried weighing the items several times. Older reviews found the scale to be accurate, but something has changed with more recent manufacturing. Piece of junk!If I could give negative stars I would. I ordered this scale march 1 and it was fine for the first month and a half or so. Cut to a couple of weeks ago and I noticed it giving wildly inaccurate readings (ie saying 1/3 of a frozen pizza only weighed 50something grams) so I change the batteries and it seems like it’s working normally. This week it’s doing the same thing being all over the place with weights. I wish I hadn’t thrown away my old trusty scale when I got this cute new one.Does not work if there is any fluid on your finger when pressing the "buttons" or fluid on the scale (not actual buttons you press because they are under glass). This was a replacement for a previous model by same mfg.

Note: March 2025 Nicewell customer service reached out to me and offered a refund based on my review. This is customer service at it's finest.
If there was another model I would purchase it but there is not. My previous Nicewell scale worked perfectly. The glass top is the problem since any moisture on scale or fingertips prevents it from functioning.Click to play video
I've been using this scale for a couple of months now and can honestly say it is far from my favorite kitchen scale I've ever had. I do like the high capacity, but that's about it.

PROS:
High capacity

CONS:
The finish on the scale has not held up at all to normal use. (see photo)
The buttons are part of the weighing platform so it is hard to press them without it registering a weight change and thereby ignoring that you are trying to press a button.
The buttons are sensitive to any moisture so even a drip of water on one of them can cause the scale to change mode, tare, or even power off.

BIGGEST CON:
The scale is ridiculously sensitive to any vibration. You can see in the included video that just me blowing on the scale causes the reading to fluctuate. Even someone walking across the room causes the reading to fluctuate so every time my husband walks into the kitchen while I am using the scale, I have to stop what I am doing and wait for him to stop moving around.

Overall, the scale works (and I am outside the return window) so I will keep using it but I definitely would not recommend it.I keep hoping that these things will work. This worked well for a couple days. And then noticed odd glitches. Weights would change by 2 or more grams while watching. Tare function is touchy. The batteries were new out of the box.

It's disappointing because it has such a pleasant design and it's large. It was to replace a smaller one I've had since about 2005. An Escali P115C. It never malfunctioned. Only had to replace infrequently. The Escali is good for baking because most ingredients are placed in bowls which fit easily on it. BUT this Nicewell scale has a much larger area to place loose vegetables on. Guess I'll just go back to the Escali with a platter on top.This scale was awesome for about a month. After the first month, the scale is VERY laggy . I’ll be dumping ingredients for my dough and it will randomly jump 1-5 grams out of nowhere. The tare button pretty much needs to be pressed as hard as possible for it to actually work. I tried changing batteries and it still doesn’t work properly. I put the same nickel on it three times and the weight was 4g, 5g, and 6g. It should weigh 5 grams every time. I was excited for this scale when I got it but now it is useless. Of course the return window is now closed so I’m stuck with this dumb thing that is pretty much useless. Get a different scale.
